latin: Quarumcunque uirtutum naturalium uel diuinarum eadem est proprietatis analogia, idem etiam nomen, idem hymnus, idem opus, seruata proportione. Et qui tentauerit exponere uidebit correspondentiam.
translation: Whatever the natural or divine powers may be, their analogy of property is the same, and so too the name, the hymn, and the work belonging to each, proportion being preserved; whoever attempts to expound this will perceive the correspondence.
translation_note: This rendering is prepared independently from the Latin; Howlett separately quotes Farmer's own published translation of the sentence together with the Latin in her discussion of the thesis (howlett2021:6221).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch17, from Latin at farmer1998:25680
doctrine: The thesis states a principle of universal analogical correspondence linking name, hymn, and operative work for each natural or divine power (farmer1998:25680). Farmer groups this thesis with 10>7 as expressing 'Pico's extreme correlative system' (farmer1998:25762).
historiography: Howlett quotes the thesis, giving both Farmer's English and the Latin, and in the same note cites Wirszubski 1989 at page 261, without further detail in the material consulted (howlett2021:6221).
not_established: The substance of Wirszubski's discussion, cited by Howlett at 1989, p. 261, is not given in the material consulted beyond the page citation (howlett2021:6221).
